reason: The court accepted the fundamental-breach limitation, but the statement omits the material requirement that the breach be imputable to the contracting party personally and the cited CPC section was not construed for this rule.
The quote is the District Judge's reproduced finding and the appellate court held there was no proper proof that the will had been admitted to probate.
The statement is a vague paraphrase and misses the actual holding on an established charitable trust of public character under the exemption provision.
The court did not hold that income is needed for a trust to be validly established, but that exempt income must be income of an established charitable trust.
The quoted passage supports the holding that a charitable trust must benefit the public or a section of the public.
The quote reproduces trial-level findings and the appellate ratio was instead that an administrator cannot be made to account for property not received qua administrator.
This is a fact-specific item from the lower court's accounting order, which the appellate court set aside rather than adopted as a legal rule.
The court made a narrow evidentiary comparison on the facts, including an attesting witness, not a general rule that reliability is determined by original or certified documents.
The quote directly supports the holding that an unpleaded mixed question of fact and law cannot be raised for the first time in appeal.
The quote supports a fact-specific finding that the copies differed, but that finding is not itself the legal ratio of the case.
The court held that signatures taken on blank notarial forms later filled meant there was no due execution of the deed.
The quoted passage supports the holding that the court could act on an illegality in a notarial document disclosed by the evidence.
The quote directly states the probate rule that the party propounding the will bears the onus of proving it.
The burden is on the propounder of the will, not on the testator, so the statement reverses the legal actor.
The statement captures the general rule but omits the court's material qualification that suspicious circumstances require the propounder to remove the suspicion.
The quote supports the holding that possession under an acknowledged limited right will not become adverse until that limited character is shed.
The quote directly supports the jurisdictional holding after a section 284 reference to the District Court.
The quoted holding concerns the Public Trustee's lack of jurisdiction pending the District Court reference, not a party's opportunity to be heard.
The quote directly supports the holding that section 295 cannot be used while a court reference is pending.
The supporting passage is largely a quotation of another case and the majority disposed of the appeal on mens rea while reserving the parate-execution validity issue.
The statement comes from a quoted Oudh decision that the present court distinguished, not from this court's own holding.
The court did use consent as a distinguishing observation, but it was not the majority ratio because the appeal turned on bona fide claim of right and absence of dishonest intent.
The court held that an assignment of an existing mortgage was valid precisely because it was not a voluntary alienation of an interest in the land, so the statement is misleading.
The headnote and final order support the majority holding that section 24 does not bar injunctions for ministerial acts alleged to be without jurisdiction, ultra vires, or in bad faith.
The majority holding states that once importation is proved section 152 shifts the burden of proving lawful importation to the claimant.
